title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1982-04-05
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) ->
source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony D5M/Maxell DXLIIS/Dolby B) D

ai_review.summary: Brilliant audience recording captures a high‑energy set with standout Friend of the Devil and an electric Bertha > Playin' > Ship sequence.
ai_review.review: The audience tape is praised for its clear, immersive sound that puts listeners right in the hall, while the performance shines on the first set and the Bertha‑Playin’‑Ship jam in the second. Jerry’s voice and guitar work are highlighted as strong, and several songs (Friend of the Devil, Althea, Deep Elem) receive special mention. A few reviewers note a rough start to the second set, but overall the show is regarded as solid and exciting.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both the performance and the audience recording; only a few lower comments exist, so the weighted average leans strongly positive.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers call the tape brilliant, crisp and beautiful; one notes it isn’t high‑qual compared to a possible SBD but is the best available, with no major dropouts reported.

standout_songs: Bertha > Playin' in the Band > Ship of Fools
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as solid and money‑making; second set features a wild, lengthy jam from Bertha into Playin' and Ship leading into Drums, with a looser but exciting flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice is praised on Friend of the Devil and Ship of Fools; guitar work described as firing on eight cylinders.
band_member_comments.Drums: The post‑Ship jam into Drums is highlighted for its unique, extended excursion with Brent and Bobby keeping the momentum.
